key_insight: UniIntervene reduces the need for constant human corrections in real-world reinforcement learning by using an agentic intervention model that can detect unproductive behavior and step in more efficiently. This makes human-in-the-loop robotic learning more scalable and less labor-intensive.
problem_solved: Current human-in-the-loop RL systems for robotic manipulation require frequent manual interventions to steer policies away from ineffective exploration, creating high labor cost and limiting practical deployment at scale.
method: Introduces an agentic intervention model that monitors learning behavior and identifies when the policy is heading toward unproductive exploration.
Triggers targeted interventions only when needed, reducing unnecessary human involvement while preserving learning efficiency.
Designed for real-world robotic manipulation settings where online policy improvement must be both effective and labor-efficient.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach points to a more scalable way to train robots in the real world with less human supervision. It could lower annotation and intervention costs while improving the practicality of human-guided reinforcement learning systems.

paper_title: UniIntervene: Agentic Intervention for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Haoyuan Deng, Yitong Gao, Yudong Lin, Haichao Liu, Zhenyu Wu
